Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=5{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(x+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-1$, $x=0.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=-1$ to $x=0.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}x(5{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =10\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({x}^{4}+{x}^{3})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=16x-16{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}16x-16{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3} & =0 \\ 4x({x}^{2}-4x+4) & =0 \\ 4x(x-2)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(16x-16{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(16{x}^{2}-16{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =8\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+{x}^{4})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the finite region bounded between the curves $y=3-x$ and $y={x}^{2}-6x+9.$ Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=3-x$ and $g(x)={x}^{2}-6x+9.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 3-x & ={x}^{2}-6x+9 \\ {x}^{2}-5x+6 & =0 \\ (x-2)(x-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=2$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=2$ to $x=3.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14261267/assets/b793d15c35fdd668e988459bcfe6c3978eab822c57bfe0fabde463e68e69c04e.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)={x}^{2}-6x+9,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=3-x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}x([3-x]-[{x}^{2}-6x+9])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}x(-{x}^{2}+5x-6)\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}(-{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}-6x)\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}-3{x}^{2})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =2\pi [(-\frac{81}{4}+45-27)-(-4+\frac{40}{3}-12)] \\  & =2\pi (-\frac{9}{4}-(-\frac{8}{3})) \\  & =2\pi \cdot \frac{5}{12} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=2x$ and $g(x)=5x-{x}^{2}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 2x & =5x-{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}-3x & =0 \\ x(x-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=3.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14261267/assets/356b505e3a638cd83d83a82c69a2a70619d6036d238959cf5aa655980d23af3e.png)

  

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=2x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=5x-{x}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}x([5x-{x}^{2}]-[2x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}x(3x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {({x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =2\pi [(27-\frac{81}{4})-0] \\  & =\frac{27\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
